raw:
The Brixham was a steam collier that arrived at Newcastle on 12 October 1884, completing a six-day voyage from London during which she carried 640 tons of coal. Her master, Captain Elias Ward, reported that the ship encountered strong headwinds off Flamborough Head on the second day of the passage, which cost the vessel nearly ten hours of travelling time.

The Brixham had been built in 1879 at Middlesbrough and was registered at 812 tons gross. Her engines developed 900 indicated horsepower and burned twenty-two tons of coal per day. She was owned by Temperley and Carter of London, who intended her for the regular coal run between the Tyne and the capital.

On this voyage the ship carried a crew of twenty-two men together with three officers. Before departure, two firemen had been discharged at London for drunkenness, and the men who replaced them were signed on only hours before the ship left the dock. The cargo was delivered in good order, and the surveyor's certificate recorded that there was no damage to the hatches or coamings.

**Record of the Cape Verde Point Lighthouse Text**

The text describes the lighthouse at Cape Verde Point, beginning with its establishment and continuing through its operational details, safety additions, and staffing history.

The lighthouse was commissioned on 3 March 1901 and was first lit by its keeper, Augusto Ferreira. Ferreira remained in charge of the light for eleven consecutive years. The tower itself rises to a height of 34 metres. Its light is produced by a dioptric apparatus of the second order, which displays two white flashes every fifteen seconds. This light can be seen from a distance of 18 nautical miles.

In terms of operation, the station burns kerosene as its fuel, consuming it at a rate of 460 litres per month. The kerosene is kept in a store that was built into the head keeper's cottage.

A fog signal was added to the station in 1904, producing two blasts per minute. This addition came about as a direct consequence of a maritime disaster: the wreck of the barque Santa Ana. The Santa Ana had struck the reef beneath the point on 9 July 1903, and seven hands were lost in the wreck.

Regarding the surrounding geography and communications, the point lies 6 kilometres north of the fishing port of Praia Seca. A telephone line connecting the station to that port was completed in 1907.

The text concludes with a change of staffing: Ferreira was succeeded in 1912 by his assistant, Joao Braz. Braz had joined the lighthouse service in 1898, meaning he had been in the service for some fourteen years before taking over the position.

**Record of the Cape Verde Point Lighthouse Text**

The text describes the lighthouse at Cape Verde Point, beginning with its establishment and continuing through its operational details, safety additions, and staffing history.

The lighthouse was commissioned on 3 March 1901 and was first lit by its keeper, Augusto Ferreira. Ferreira remained in charge of the light for eleven consecutive years. The tower itself rises to a height of 34 metres. Its light is produced by a dioptric apparatus of the second order, which displays two white flashes every fifteen seconds. This light can be seen from a distance of 18 nautical miles.

In terms of operation, the station burns kerosene as its fuel, consuming it at a rate of 460 litres per month. The kerosene is kept in a store that was built into the head keeper's cottage.

A fog signal was added to the station in 1904, producing two blasts per minute. This addition came about as a direct consequence of a maritime disaster: the wreck of the barque Santa Ana. The Santa Ana had struck the reef beneath the point on 9 July 1903, and seven hands were lost in the wreck.

Regarding the surrounding geography and communications, the point lies 6 kilometres north of the fishing port of Praia Seca. A telephone line connecting the station to that port was completed in 1907.

The text concludes with a change of staffing: Ferreira was succeeded in 1912 by his assistant, Joao Braz. Braz had joined the lighthouse service in 1898, meaning he had been in the service for some fourteen years before taking over the position.

TELEPHONE LINE PORT COMPLETED 1907. FERREIRA SUCCEEDED 1912 BY ASSISTANT JOAO BRAZ, JOINED SERVICE 1898.
